name: Retractable Claw Modification
description: Replaces the fingernails with retractable claws housed in modified nail beds. In retracted position, the claws lie flat and appear as slightly thick, curved fingernails. When deployed through a flexion trigger in the fingertips, they extend 2–3 cm beyond the fingertip — curved, sharp, and strong enough to score wood, leather, and light metal. The claws are keratinous like fingernails but significantly denser, with a self-sharpening growth pattern that maintains the edge. They're not weapons capable of penetrating body armor, but in close combat they're effective slashing tools. The modification is popular in the Shelf as a discreet self-defense option that requires no equipment and can't be confiscated. Combined with cat ears and a tail, the claws complete a feline body modification suite that a significant portion of GLMZ's population has adopted.
source_organism: Felis catus (domestic cat), Panthera onca (jaguar, enhanced claw density)
procedure: Fingertip surgery with retractable claw induction, 1 session per hand
expression_time: 4–6 weeks for claw growth; retraction mechanism functional at 8 weeks
reversibility: Reversible with nail bed reconstruction; normal nails regrow over 3 months
side_effects: Claws click on hard surfaces when not fully retracted
Touchscreen and fine manipulation impaired when claws are partially deployed
Claw sheaths ache in cold weather
Accidental deployment during gripping — scratching partners, damaging clothing, scoring furniture
Claws must be maintained — broken claws are painful and take weeks to regrow
social_perception: Common and unremarkable in the Shelf. Cat claws are part of the feline modification package that defines GLMZ's aesthetic. Corporate environments require claws to remain retracted. In practice, most claw users deploy them so rarely that the modification is invisible in daily life.
story_hooks: A claw user's keratin composition is altered by a contaminated gene package — their claws are now producing a mild paralytic compound on their edges, a feature that wasn't in the installation spec
Claw marks at a crime scene are analyzed for keratin protein signature, identifying the attacker as definitively as a fingerprint — retractable claws leave unique trace evidence
